issues.description: The solution implementation declares lecture attributes using snake_case names (e.g. lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students) but the constructor and all methods reference camelCase field names (e.g. lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents). This internal name mismatch in the solution causes compile errors and contradicts the UML and problem description which use camelCase attribute names. Students reading the solution or comparing to the UML will be confused about the intended attribute identifiers and cannot rely on the solution as a correct reference.
issues.suggestedFix: Align attribute declarations and usage: rename the fields in the solution to match the UML/camelCase identifiers (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) or update all constructor parameters and method references to use the declared snake_case names consistently. Preferably use the camelCase names from the UML so template, tests and solution are coherent.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify attributes with camelCase names (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). In the solution implementation the private fields are declared with snake_case identifiers (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) while the rest of the solution (constructor, getters/setters, toString, etc.) uses camelCase names (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, ...). This creates a mismatch across artifacts and within the solution code itself, breaking the direct mapping students expect from the UML to the implementation and causing a compilation / comprehension issue.
issues.suggestedFix: Use consistent camelCase attribute names that match the UML and the rest of the code. Rename the private fields in the solution to: private String lectureName; private int numberOfInscribedStudents; private int numberOfGuestStudents; private int numberOfLecturers; private int numberOfTutors; (or alternatively, change all usages to the chosen snake_case style) so that declaration and usage align and match the problem statement.
